pages.text:
Burns liquid fuel into heat, but never hotter than the fuel burns:
- Creosote: 60 HU/t, up to 850°C.
- Naphtha: 200 HU/t, up to 1,200°C.
- Light Oil: 125 HU/t, up to 1,000°C.
- Heavy Oil: 50 HU/t, up to 750°C.
Superheated Steam needs a 900°C boiler, so a creosote burner only reaches High-Pressure: distil the creosote into Naphtha for that. Switching to a cooler fuel lets it cool down to that fuel's temperature.
- Hydrogen (a gas, from the Electrolyzer): 60 HU/t, up to 1,400°C. Feed it with a Pressurized Conduit, a Cylinder or a Gas Cartridge.
- Biodiesel (from Seed Oil and Ethanol): 160 HU/t, up to 1,000°C.
- Biogas (a gas, from the Biogas Digester): 45 HU/t, up to 1,100°C.
Feed it oxygen for oxy-fuel: see Oxy-Fuel.
Set a face to Flue Gas and it gives off Carbon Dioxide through it while it burns carbon fuels: see Carbon Capture.
